sourcedFrom: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: A 4 inch, 2 inch diameter duty can for 5.56 only, built as a SOLID 3D PRINTED body — 14.1 oz in Inconel, or 8.6 oz as the Speed K Ti in titanium — on an industry standard HUB mount. ⛔ It does not come apart. The baffles cannot be removed and the only component that detaches is the mount interface, so every cleaning operation Banish publishes happens with the can intact. It also has 4 vent ports in the muzzle cap that have to be rodded out by hand.

steps.title: Clear the host, using the host's own manual
steps.action: Unload the rifle and lock the action open so the chamber is visibly clear before the can is touched. Banish prints no clearing sequence and refers you to your own firearm's manual — which on a 5.56 duty gun means magazine out and bolt locked back before anything else.
steps.prose: This is a can built for people who carry a rifle for a living. It goes on and off in circumstances where the habit matters more than the checklist.
steps.quote: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: The host firearm's manual is the clearing authority.

steps.title: Speed K is 5.56 only
steps.action: Check the host chambering. The SPECS block gives CALIBER .223/5.56 and CALIBER RANGE .223/5.56 — the range and the caliber are the same entry, which is Banish's way of saying there is no span here. It is fully auto rated, and the Inconel body is what earns that.
steps.prose: A 2 inch diameter can that is only 4 inches long has very little room inside it. The narrow rating is the design, not a limitation of the paperwork.
steps.quote: The BANISH® Speed K is a 5.56 caliber silencer with clipped-wall baffles and a finned blast chamber that ensures maximum sound reduction while maintaining optimal performance.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: ⛔ Not user-serviceable — the baffles do not come out
steps.action: Know this before you look for a tool. The Speed K is a solid 3D printed construction: the baffles cannot be removed, and the ONLY part that can be taken off for cleaning is the mount interface. There is no end cap procedure, no baffle count you can act on and no torque figure for an internal joint, because there is no internal joint.
steps.prose: Banish's own SPECS line reads SELF-SERVICE: NO. Anything that looks like a seam on this can is a printed feature, not a fastener.
steps.aside: 'bre removed' is the publisher's typo, quoted as printed.
steps.quote: The BANISH Speed K is not user-serviceable, it is a solid 3D printed construction and the baffles cannot be removed. The only part that can bre removed for cleaning is the mount interface.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6
steps.warn: Sealed can. Do not attempt to open it.

steps.title: Check the mount is fully shouldered before firing
steps.action: Confirm the thread mount is fully shouldered with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the mount, and that any crush washer from an earlier muzzle device has been removed. On a 4 inch can there is no length for a misalignment to correct itself over.
steps.prose: A HUB can is only as square as its mount, and this mount is doing the whole job on its own.
steps.quote: Check the fit between your barrel and silencer before firing! The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool — an Inconel duty can holds a lot of heat
steps.action: After firing, use extreme caution: Banish tells you the can may be hot to the touch and offers a Devour suppressor cover or gloves. The Speed K is fully auto rated, so the round counts that get it hot are exactly the ones it is designed for.
steps.prose: Inconel was chosen partly for lower heat retention, but lower is not low. A 2 inch diameter body has a lot of surface right where your hand goes.
steps.quote: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Cover or gloves after any sustained string.

steps.title: Take the Speed K off the host, then take the mount out of the can
steps.action: Remove the can from the firearm first, then unthread the mount interface from the back of the can. That mount is the ONLY thing that separates from this suppressor, and Banish requires it to come out as part of every clean so its internal and external threads can be reached.
steps.prose: Banish's own cleaning instruction is explicit that the mount must come out. Skipping it leaves the threads that hold the whole thing on the gun uncleaned.
steps.caution: The mount is the only removable component. Nothing else.
steps.quote: Ensure to remove the mount and thoroughly clean the threads of any debris or buildup.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Clean both sets of threads — the can's and the mount's
steps.action: With the mount out, clean the suppressor's own threads AND the mount's internal and external threads. Three thread surfaces, not one. Carbon in any of them is what stops the mount seating square, and a mount that does not seat square puts a 5.56 bullet into a 4 inch can with clipped-wall baffles.
steps.prose: Banish spells the three surfaces out rather than saying 'clean the threads', which is a hint about how often only one of them gets done.
steps.quote: This should be done for both the silencer threads, as well as the mount’s internal, and external, threads.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Rod the four vent ports in the muzzle cap
steps.action: This can has 4 vent ports in the muzzle cap and they need a rod run down them to push out debris and carbon. They are part of the controlled-flow design that keeps blowback down to the stated 5.8 percent increase, so a blocked port is a performance change as well as a fouling problem.
steps.prose: Nothing else in the Banish line has this step, because nothing else in the line vents the muzzle cap.
steps.quote: And you will need to run a rod down the 4x vent ports in the muzzle cap to push out any debris/carbon that may have built up.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Speed K is off the host with the mount out — and that is the entire strip, because the body is one printed piece. Banish sets the cleaning interval at every 50 to 100 rounds and warns off solid lead or plated lead bullets. Everything further is a soak, which is what the Deep Clean covers.
steps.prose: Never fire this can with anything in it: Banish's obstruction rule applies with force to a can you cannot open to check.
steps.quote: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: You cannot inspect the inside of this can by taking it apart. Sight through it.

deepSteps.title: Two published soak methods — pick one, 24 hours either way
deepSteps.action: Banish gives two ways in. Either submerge the whole can in a dish soap solution, or seal the muzzle exit hole and fill the silencer with cleaning solution. Whichever you choose, it sits for 24 hours. Any firearm solvent or sonic wash cleaning solution will work.
deepSteps.prose: The fill-and-seal method is the one that reaches the blast chamber properly on a can this short, because a soak bath will not get past the trapped air otherwise.
deepSteps.quote: Soak the entire can in a dish soap solution OR seal the muzzle exit hole and fill the silencer with any cleaning solution and let it sit for 24hrs in both scenarios.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Nothing that strips Cerakote
deepSteps.action: Check the solution before the can goes in it. Banish forbids anything that will strip the Cerakote coating from the silencer. On a duty can the finish is corrosion protection, not decoration, and Inconel with the coating removed will discolour and pit where the gas hits it.
deepSteps.prose: That rules out a lot of aggressive carbon removers and most paint-stripping degreasers. Read the solvent's label, not just the gun-cleaning aisle it came from.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote coating from the silencer.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: Brass brush on the blast chamber and accuracy baffle
deepSteps.action: Once the soak is done, take a brass brush to the blast chamber and the accuracy baffle — those are the two internal features Banish names, and they are the two you can actually reach from either end of a sealed can. Everything else is behind them and stays where it is.
deepSteps.prose: Brass, not steel. The body is printed Inconel or titanium and the finned blast chamber has thin features in it.
deepSteps.quote: Once soaked, take a brass brush, and clean the blast chamber and accuracy baffle.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: Dry it fully, refit the mount, then fire 10-15 fouling rounds
deepSteps.action: Let the silencer dry completely before the mount goes back in. Then re-install the mount and put 10 to 15 rounds through it: Banish's own reasoning is that the high pressure shoots out the loose debris and buildup the cleaning loosened but did not remove.
deepSteps.prose: That last part is unusual and it is deliberate. On a can you cannot open, the pressure IS the final cleaning step.
deepSteps.quote: Once clean, allow the silencer to dry. Re-install the mount and you are ready to shoot again. Shoot 10 - 15 rounds through the silencer. The high pressure will shoot out any loose debris and buildup that was loosened during cleaning.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH SPEED K — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — CLEANING, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Fully dry before firing. A can with solvent still in it is obstructed.

cleaning.name: SOAK
tasks: Either submerge the can in a dish soap solution, or seal the muzzle exit and fill it with cleaning solution
Use nothing that will strip the Cerakote coating
Any firearm solvent or sonic wash cleaning solution is acceptable within that limit

cleaning.name: REACHABLE INTERNALS
tasks: Brass brush the blast chamber and the accuracy baffle
Run a rod down all 4 vent ports in the muzzle cap
Do not attempt to remove baffles — the body is a single 3D printed piece

cleaning.name: MOUNT AND THREADS
tasks: Remove the mount interface — it is the only removable component
Clean the mount's internal threads AND its external threads
Refit the mount only once everything is dry

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: Allow the silencer to dry completely
Fire 10 to 15 rounds to blow out debris the cleaning loosened
Do not use solid lead or plated lead bullets

reassembly: Confirm the can is completely dry inside before anything is refitted.
Thread the mount interface back into the rear of the suppressor.
Fit the can to the host and confirm the mount is fully shouldered with no visible gap.
Fire 10 to 15 rounds so the pressure clears any debris the cleaning loosened.
fncheck: Sight straight through the Speed K from the mount end and confirm one clear channel with no standing solvent — on a sealed can that view is the only internal inspection available. Check all four muzzle-cap vent ports are open. Confirm the mount is threaded home and that the can sits square on the host with no gap at the shoulder, then put the first 10 to 15 rounds through it as Banish's fouling sequence.
